transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the quarter-end purchase-accounting review for the software acquisition we closed on September 30th. The draft package currently shows $18 million in provisional goodwill, and I need to walk through the open items with each of you before I can sign off. I'd like to hear from valuation, tax, legal, and audit liaison on where things stand and what adjustments or disclosure actions still need to be captured in the package. Please go ahead.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed the customer-relationship valuation this morning. I've confirmed that $6,400,000 must be recognized as an identifiable customer-relationship intangible asset with an 8-year useful life. My valuation memo hasn't been attached to the close file yet, but I'm committing to incorporating it. This means the provisional goodwill of $18 million should be reduced by $6.4 million, bringing it down to $11.6 million, with the customer-relationship intangible recognized separately and amortized over 8 years.

transcript.text: I need to flag a tax item. I confirmed in a tax memo received this morning that the customer-relationship asset has a zero tax basis and the applicable enacted tax rate is 21%, which requires recognizing a $1,344,000 deferred tax liability. This memo has not yet been circulated to financial reporting. This deferred tax liability needs to be captured as a purchase-accounting adjustment in the package, and it will also affect the goodwill calculation since the deferred tax liability increases the net liabilities assumed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I reviewed the signed purchase agreement this week and confirmed that a $2,100,000 employee-retention earnout is probable and payable in 2027, so it must be recorded as contingent consideration in the purchase-accounting package. My contract summary is still in the legal deal folder, but I'm committing to incorporating this adjustment. This contingent consideration liability will also affect the goodwill calculation since it increases the consideration transferred.

First, the transaction is material and requires an acquisition-date pro forma revenue disclosure. Second, a sensitivity disclosure for the earnout is also required. Both disclosures must be filed within 5 business days after sign-off. One more thing — the audit planning memo itself has not yet been added to the reporting checklist, so we need to make sure that happens. These disclosure actions should be captured in the package before Elena signs off.
